attributes.name: Configuration
attributes.description: What is actually in the box. The most commercially consequential field in this cohort: the same tool as a bare unit and as a kit differ by roughly 3x in price because one includes a battery and charger, and the values below are the words suppliers print rather than a tidy scheme of our own.

allowed_values.note: batteries and charger without a tool

attributes.name: Power Source
attributes.description: What drives the tool. The first thing a buyer filters on and the thing that decides whether a battery platform is even relevant, so it is recorded even when it seems obvious from the product name.

attributes.name: Battery Platform
attributes.description: The manufacturer's battery system name, recorded verbatim. A string rather than an enum because the value set is proprietary and open-ended, and because these names are not reducible to voltage: M18 and 18V LXT are both 18 V and neither battery fits the other tool.

attributes.name: Battery Voltage
attributes.description: Nominal battery voltage. Distinct from voltage_rating, which is the mains supply a corded tool expects, and distinct from battery_platform, which is the interface. Stated separately because it is the figure that predicts power while the platform predicts fit.

attributes.name: Drive Size
attributes.description: The output drive a powered driver, wrench or ratchet presents. A string because the values mix square-drive fractions with hex designations — 1/2" square and 1/4" hex are different interfaces that a bare fraction could not distinguish.

attributes.name: Chuck Size
attributes.description: Maximum shank diameter the chuck accepts, which caps the bit size the tool can hold. Distinct from drive_size: a drill has a chuck, an impact wrench has an anvil.

attributes.name: Blade Diameter
attributes.description: Outside diameter of a circular saw blade, or the blade a saw is built to take. Recorded separately from wheel_diameter because a toothed blade and a bonded wheel are different products whose sizes must not be pooled into one column.

attributes.name: No-Load Speed (RPM)
attributes.description: Maximum unloaded output speed in revolutions per minute. Declared as a plain integer because RPM is a rate the unit registry does not carry. A multi-speed tool states a range; record the top figure and put the full range in additional_information.

attributes.name: Voltage Rating
attributes.description: Nominal supply voltage the appliance is designed to operate on. Read the nameplate or electrical-specification row, not the motor or component rating, which may differ.

attributes.name: Amperage Rating
attributes.description: Rated current draw at the nominal supply voltage. Determines the branch circuit the appliance requires, so it is a fitment attribute rather than a performance one.

attributes.name: Product Series
attributes.description: Manufacturer's series or family designation only, without the word "series" and without the manufacturer name. The anchor for part-number grammar induction, because the positional encoding of a smart part number is defined per series rather than per manufacturer.

attributes.name: Model
attributes.description: The manufacturer's marketing model designation where it differs from the ordering part number. Often absent, or identical to the MPN and therefore not restated by the manufacturer, which is why the ground truth leaves it blank.

attributes.name: Size
attributes.description: The manufacturer's headline size statement, kept as published with its axis labels intact, e.g. "24 in W x 24-1/4 in D". Deliberately a string and not a dimension_set: the published form varies in both the number of axes and their order, and the client's ground truth carries no unit column for it, so reformatting into a fixed W x H x D triple would discard information and diverge from the expected output.

attributes.name: Weight (Each)
attributes.description: Shipping weight of a single unit. Distinguish carefully from carton weight; datasheets often place them in adjacent columns with similar headings.

attributes.name: Sound Level
attributes.description: A-weighted sound pressure level during normal operation, as published by the manufacturer. Lower is quieter. Record the figure for the standard or normal cycle when several cycles are rated, and never convert an unweighted dB figure into dBA — the two are not interconvertible without the signal spectrum.

attributes.name: Pack Quantity
attributes.description: Number of units in the consumer pack the part number sells as. Distinct from case_quantity, which counts packs in a shipping carton: a "3pk" of lamps is one sellable unit containing three lamps, and confusing the two misprices the line.

attributes.name: Selling Unit of Measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the product is sold, which is not necessarily the unit in which it is priced or stocked. Conflating the three is a classic source of order errors.

attributes.name: Additional Information
attributes.description: Comma-separated residual specifications the class has no dedicated attribute for, in the client's own overflow convention, e.g. "240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours". A holding pen, not a dumping ground: anything appearing here repeatedly across a category is a missing attribute and should be promoted to one.
example_values: 240 kW-hr Annual Energy, 1 to 12 hr Delay Start Hours
Folding Tines, Leak Detection System, Normal Cycle

attributes.name: Power Input
attributes.description: Electrical power the tool draws from the supply, in watts. This is consumption and not output: a 1000 W motor does not deliver 1000 W of work. Never record a voltage or a current here even when the spec table places them adjacent.

attributes.name: Mains Frequency
attributes.description: Supply frequency the tool accepts. The dual "50/60 Hz" rating is the fact that decides whether a 50 Hz machine can be sold into a 60 Hz market at all, so it is recorded as its own value rather than reduced to one of the two figures.

attributes.name: Cable Length
attributes.description: Length of the fitted mains cable, which sets the working radius before an extension lead is needed. Distinct from hose length on an extractor and from any overall dimension.

attributes.name: Airflow
attributes.description: Maximum volume of air the tool moves per unit time, measured at the inlet with no hose. Read together with suction_pressure: airflow carries the dust away once it is airborne, suction is what lifts it. Manufacturers publish this in l/min, m3/h or cfm interchangeably, so the figures are not comparable until converted.

attributes.name: Vacuum
attributes.description: Maximum negative pressure the tool develops with the inlet sealed, which sets how well it lifts heavy debris and how far it tolerates a long or clogged hose. Published as "vacuum", "suction" or a water-lift figure; all three describe the same quantity.

attributes.name: Dust Container Volume
attributes.description: Capacity of the collection container or bag, which decides how long the machine runs before it is emptied. Distinct from each_weight and from the machine's overall size: a compact body can carry a large tank.

attributes.name: Dust Class
attributes.description: European filtration class under EN 60335-2-69, which is a legal fitness test rather than a quality grade: L passes nuisance dust, M is required for wood and most construction dust, and H is required for asbestos and carcinogens. Substituting downward is a compliance failure, not a lesser specification, so this is never interchangeable.

attributes.name: Height
attributes.description: Overall height of the product as it stands, excluding a detachable handle or hose. Recorded separately from overall_size for the datasheets that tabulate each dimension on its own row.

attributes.name: Length
attributes.description: Overall length of the product along its longest horizontal axis. Recorded separately from overall_size for the datasheets that tabulate each dimension on its own row.

attributes.name: Width
attributes.description: Overall width of the product across its shortest horizontal axis. Recorded separately from overall_size for the datasheets that tabulate each dimension on its own row.

attributes.name: Warranty
attributes.description: Warranty coverage as stated by the manufacturer, including duration and what it covers, e.g. "1 Year Manufacturer, 1 Year Labor and Parts". Recorded as published: summarising it into a single duration loses the parts/labour distinction that determines what a claim actually pays for.
example_values: 1 Year Manufacturer, 1 Year Labor and Parts

attributes.name: Included Technology
attributes.description: Named proprietary technology the product ships with, phrased as the client's "With" column expects it, e.g. "With CleanBoost(TM)". Trademarked feature names, so they are reproduced exactly as the manufacturer writes them including the symbol, and never paraphrased or expanded.
example_values: With Washing 3rd Rack, Water Repellent Basket

attributes.name: Approvals and Listings
attributes.description: Third-party certifications, listings and approvals explicitly stated in the source. Record only what is stated. A listing number without a recognised mark is not an approval, and an approval for one size in a series does not extend to the others.

allowed_values.note: Generic NSF mark with no standard named. Deliberately not aliased onto NSF-61: a potable-water claim needs the specific standard, and treating this as equivalent would let a cross-field rule pass on evidence that does not support it.
eye and face protection impact rating
hand protection cut, abrasion and puncture rating
building-code evaluation report for a structural or envelope product
composite decking and railing performance standard

attributes.name: Country of Origin
attributes.description: Country where the product is manufactured, as stated by the manufacturer. Drives tariff treatment and trade-agreement eligibility, so a guess here has direct financial consequences.

attributes.name: California Prop 65 Warning Required
attributes.description: True when the source states that a California Proposition 65 warning applies. Absence of a statement is not evidence of absence of a requirement, so record a gap rather than false when the source is silent.

attributes.name: GTIN / UPC
attributes.description: Global Trade Item Number, 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits. The final digit is a modulo-10 check digit, which L0 validation verifies arithmetically — a transposed digit is therefore detectable without any external lookup.

cross_field_rules.expr: power_source != 'Cordless (Battery)' or battery_platform is not null
cross_field_rules.message: A cordless tool was captured with no battery platform. The platform is the compatibility fact a buyer needs — an M18 battery does not fit an 18V LXT tool despite both being eighteen volts — so a cordless listing without it is not orderable by anyone who owns batteries already.

A corded or pneumatic tool is described as a bare tool. "Bare" means no battery and no charger, which is only a meaningful distinction on a cordless product; on a corded one it usually means a word was matched out of context.

cross_field_rules.expr: power_source != 'Corded Electric' or battery_platform is null
cross_field_rules.message: A battery platform was recorded against a corded tool. Usually means a voltage token such as "120V" was read as a platform name, which would then assert compatibility with a battery system the tool cannot accept.
